title: Naples 1880 catalogue ↔ surviving St Andrews slides: object-side candidate extraction
status: candidate layer only; no new physical-identity closure asserted
core_rule: A taxon match or a handwritten number on a surviving slide is not a catalogue-number match until the 1880 row wording and object label are directly compared.

catalogue_number_structure.guard: These ranges derive from the parsed sequential catalogue structure and subgroup counts. They locate a candidate number taxonomically; they do not identify the preparation wording at that number.

high_priority_candidate.title: Delphinus phocaena
high_priority_candidate.observed_catalogue_description: St Andrews records a light-orange STAZIONE ZOOLOG / NAPOLI label, taxon Delphinus phocaena, and manuscript wording 'Panis 383' on the right label. Current position is pigeon-hole T8; a modern white label preserves former position 12/D/3.
high_priority_candidate.number_test: If 383 is an original Naples catalogue offering number, it falls inside the derived Mammalia band 373-405, so it is structurally plausible for Delphinus. This numerical plausibility is not an item match.
high_priority_candidate.word_test: The transcription 'Panis' is unresolved. It may encode an anatomical structure, abbreviation, personal annotation, or an OCR/cataloguing reading. Do not silently expand it to pancreas or any other organ without the historical catalogue row/image.
required_closure: Inspect the 1880 catalogue row 383 directly on the page image.
Compare taxon + anatomical preparation wording against the St Andrews label/image.
Determine whether '383' is written in a hand/layout consistent with Naples catalogue numbering on other surviving Station slides.
Check neighboring rows 382/384 and other St Andrews examples for the same label grammar.

fritz_meyer_attribution_problem.institutional_programme: The 1880 catalogue introduction establishes Fritz Meyer as organizer/director of the preparation department, not personal preparator of every catalogue item.
fritz_meyer_attribution_problem.object_side: St Andrews states that many surviving Station examples appear mounted/prepared by Fritz Meyer and preserves labels explicitly reading Prep. Fritz Meyer on some objects.
fritz_meyer_attribution_problem.business_afterlife: Other St Andrews slides use later Leipzig Fritz Meyer business labels, so the words 'Fritz Meyer' can represent different institutional/commercial phases.
fritz_meyer_attribution_problem.rule: Record 'Stazione Zoologica Napoli', 'Prep. Fritz Meyer', and later Leipzig Meyer business labels as separate attribution/address layers.

research_payoff: The Delphinus slide is a high-value test because one object may preserve an original Station identity, a possible catalogue-number trace, taxonomic/anatomical wording, and two successive St Andrews storage addresses. If row 383 closes, it would become the first surviving-object-level catalogue-number closure for the current Naples route rather than merely a programme-level match.
next: Page-image verification of catalogue row 383 is the decisive next action; do not broaden the Naples search until this cheap candidate is resolved.
